Q2 fills in the mass-balance relationship between total receipts and total demand, a hard constraint/policy that affects feasibility and whether surplus is allowed. Q3 fills in capacity limits, a constraint/boundary question. All three address unresolved assumptions in C1-C3. Q1 is the most foundational because if yard receipts are decision variables, the model's decision scope expands substantially and the objective/constraints change; if fixed, the model is a pure transportation problem. This is the highest silent-assumption risk and most changes the resulting model structure. Q2 and Q3 are also important but depend on Q1's answer. Q1 is not merely mathematically salient; it reflects a real business fact about who decides yard receipts.
